extracted.intended_audience: playwrights, dramatists, poets, and theatre practitioners interested in the use of the chorus in tragic drama
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and staging the chorus in lyrical tragedy: how it should function, be represented, and relate to diction, action, music, and the audience's experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music and rhythmical accompaniment required
rubrics_metrics.description: Music and rhythmical motion are essential accessories to the chorus; deprived of accompaniments it will appear a superfluity in the economy of the drama.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the chorus lacks musical/rhythmic support it becomes a hindrance to plot development, destructive to theatrical illusion, and wearisome to spectators. The poet should presume these accompaniments when composing lyrical tragedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Envision an ideal stage (do not be limited by present execution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transport ourselves from the actual to a possible stage; the accidental deficiency of auxiliaries ought not to confine the plastic imagination of the poet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose for the most dignified, ideal realization of the work even if present managers, actors, or venues cannot yet realize it; the poet aspires to an ideal and must allow for necessary auxiliaries in conception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the chorus to oppose naturalism and preserve poetical freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: The introduction of the chorus would be the last and decisive step ... to declare open and honorable warfare against naturalism in art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the chorus as an instrument to maintain the drama's ideal soil and poetical freedom rather than to mimic everyday reality; it guards tragedy from being subsumed by ordinary realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transform the commonplace into the poetical via the chorus
rubrics_metrics.description: The chorus transforms the commonplace actual world into the old poetical one; it enables the poet to dispense with that which is repugnant to poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the chorus to restore elevated motives, reopen palaces, and reinstate the larger-than-life surroundings necessary for poetical action rather than depicting modern quotidian settings literally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand perspective beyond immediate incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: The chorus forsakes the contracted sphere of the incidents to dilate itself over the past and the future, over distant times and nations, and general humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have the chorus step back from plot particulars to draw out general conclusions, moral lessons, and the larger human significance of events—providing reflection and universalizing the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine lyrical fancy with sensory appeal (melody & movement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chorus acts with the full power of fancy and in conjunction with the whole sensible influence of melody and rhythm, in tones and movements; it is represented by a palpable body which appeals to the senses with an imposing grandeur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design chorus passages to be both poetically elevated and sensorially effective—integrating music, song, and choreographed movement so the chorus is at once ideal and sensorially present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate reflection from incident (purifying function)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chorus keeps reflection apart from the incidents, and by this separation arms it with a poetical vigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chorus interludes to compartmentalize reflection and commentary, preventing continuous immersion in passion and thereby preserving the spectator's critical freedom and the work's poetical force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide repose to the action and preserve spectator freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: The chorus gives repose to the action; it steps between the passions with its composing views, and restores to us our freedom, which would else be lost in the tempest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ the chorus to interrupt, moderate, and compose intense dramatic sequences so the audience can detach, reflect, and avoid being overwhelmed by uninterrupted emotional intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify and permit elevated diction
rubrics_metrics.description: The lyrical effusions of the chorus impose upon the poet the necessity of a proportionate elevation of his general diction; the chorus alone entitles the poet to employ this fulness of tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When including a chorus, adopt a loftier, more majestic diction throughout; without such accompaniment such elevated language will seem forced or overstrained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance the ideal and the sensible
rubrics_metrics.description: Art can be at once altogether ideal, yet in the strictest sense real; both requisites (ideality and reality) are not contradictory but one and the same thing; the artist must not merely copy reality nor merely play with fantasy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the chorus helps achieve the equilibrium between imaginative idealization and natural truth: use idealizing treatment grounded on truthful foundations rather than mere realism or empty fancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat the chorus as a single ideal person rather than only a crowd
rubrics_metrics.description: As chorus and an ideal person it is always one and entire; I have divided it into two parts, and represented it in contest with itself; but as chorus and an ideal person it is always one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the chorus as an integrated moral/poetical voice (even when represented by many bodies). It may be split or contrasted (e.g., two-part chorus), but should not devolve into undifferentiated background noise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not degrade the chorus into a confidant
rubrics_metrics.description: The abolition of the chorus, and the debasement of this sensibly powerful organ into the characterless substitute of a confidant, is by no means such an improvement in the tragedy as the French ... would have it supposed to be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid converting the chorus into a mere personal confidant for protagonists; that is an anti-pattern which diminishes its poetical and structural function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure material/sensory elements serve ideal harmony
rubrics_metrics.description: The material, however, has its peculiar effect, and may be included in an artistical composition. But it must deserve its place by animation, fulness and harmony, and give value to the ideal forms which it surrounds instead of stifling them by its weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stagecraft, costumes, and sensory detail to enrich and support the chorus and ideals of the play—but only insofar as they animate and harmonize with the ideal forms, not overwhelm them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic license to blend religions and cultural elements
rubrics_metrics.description: I have blended together the Christian religion and the pagan mythology ... I consider it a privilege of poetry to deal with different religions as a collective whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The poet may freely adapt or combine religious or cultural motifs if they serve the poetic subject—representing the idea of the Divine in forms fitting the drama—so long as it aids the poem's ideal aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of the chorus is sometimes permissible
rubrics_metrics.description: I have also several times dispensed with its presence on the stage. For this liberty I have the example of Aeschylus ... and Sophocles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the chorus is powerful and often decisive, the dramatist may legitimately omit it in certain works or passages when such absence better serves the poetic needs, taking classical precedents into account.
